threadDescriptions.table-read: Organize and document a cast table read of Night Ferry
threadDescriptions.location-permit: Secure permission to film Night Ferry on the old ferry landing
threadDescriptions.window-blinds: Measure and replace bedroom window blinds

items.text: Night Ferry outline: the daughter reaches the landing at midnight, discovers the boat has gone, and calls her brother instead of her father.
Table read for Night Ferry: reserve the back room Thursday at seven. Need four readers, one narrator and a way to record notes.
Bedroom blind recess 112 cm wide. Measure top, middle and bottom before choosing an inside-mount kit.
Old landing permit enquiry: can a crew of six film before sunset? Ask about public access, power and who signs the location agreement.
Script revision: daughter now arrives before dusk, not midnight. Missing the last boat in daylight makes her choice visible without a long explanation.
Night Ferry read cast confirmed except the brother. Ask Dax to cover that role; the narrator can read the stage directions.
Landing office says filming access ends at 18:30. Send a plan showing crew positions and a clear pedestrian path.
Rename Night Ferry to Last Crossing on the screenplay title page. Same daughter-and-brother short, now set before dusk.
Top blind recess is only 111.4 cm. Use the narrowest measurement when ordering; 112 would jam against the frame.
Brother: You could have called. Daughter: I did. [long pause]
items.rationale: Dialogue using the established sibling characters.

items.text: Before dusk. Six or seven. Ask Dax.
items.rationale: Fragment cannot separate narrative or event logistics.

items.text: At the Last Crossing table read, the brother's second call felt repetitive. Three readers started turning pages before the daughter finished speaking, which is a useful sign that the scene had already made its point. Save their timing notes beside the read recording, with the long hesitation marked rather than trimmed out. Dax thought that pause gave the daughter time to decide whether she trusted her brother, so it should survive the edit. Cut the second call from the next screenplay draft and move its one new fact into the first call. Try the brother's admission immediately after she describes the empty landing; then let her answer with a small practical question. Keep the read's original scene numbers in the notes so we can still find the comments after renumbering the draft.
items.rationale: Preserves read documentation and specifies script edit.

items.text: Permit site sketch revised to put cables away from the public path. Crew remains six; submit the landing drawing with insurance details.
Bedroom blind sample blocks the streetlamp well but looks blue by day. Order the warmer grey in the measured recess width.
Last Crossing draft 4: first call carries the brother's admission, second call removed. End on the daughter putting the phone away, without a closing speech.
Table-read audio indexed by scene, with pauses retained for timing. Readers agreed to private sharing among the film team only.
Landing filming permission signed for 16:00–18:30. Save the countersigned agreement and bring a printed copy for the caretaker.
Grey blind installed in bedroom. Bottom rail catches the window handle; shorten the lowering limit so it clears.
Try the first one with a longer pause.
items.rationale: No explicit script, recording, or scene referent.

items.text: Last Crossing final dialogue pass: remove repeated apologies from the daughter's first call. Her hesitation before naming the landing already conveys the shame.

undo.reason: Hypothetical undo of a landing-and-time match: the source specifies a real filming permit constraint.
